items.title: The MSG 'syndrome' myth
items.claim: The idea that monosodium glutamate causes a distinctive 'Chinese restaurant syndrome' came from a 1968 letter to the New England Journal of Medicine. What does the controlled evidence show?

options.text: Robust evidence MSG causes the symptoms in most people
Double-blind trials have not consistently linked MSG within typical food levels to the reported symptoms
MSG is toxic at any dose

items.reveal_title: The popular reaction outran the evidence
items.reveal:
Reviews including the US Food and Drug Administration's classification of MSG as 'Generally Recognised As Safe' (GRAS) and double-blind challenge studies have not consistently reproduced the symptoms at dietary doses.

Kikunae Ikeda first isolated glutamate as the source of umami in 1908 at Tokyo Imperial University.
items.why: A high-profile anecdote can shape food policy and public perception for decades.

items.title: Organic vs conventional yields
items.claim: Meta-analyses have compared organic and conventional crop yields globally. What do they typically find?

options.text: Organic yields are on average around 20-25% lower with substantial variation by crop and system

items.reveal:
Seufert et al. (2012, Nature) and Ponisio et al. (2015) found organic yields averaged 19-25% lower, with smaller gaps for legumes and in some agroforestry systems.

Land-use, biodiversity and pollution trade-offs complicate any single yardstick.
items.why: Agricultural decisions involve trade-offs across multiple metrics, not a single optimisation.

items.title: Food miles vs diet choice
items.claim: Poore and Nemecek's 2018 Science analysis of food systems found transport accounts for what share of typical food carbon footprints?

options.text: Around 1-10% for most foods, with production stages dominating

items.reveal_title: Transport is usually a small slice; production dominates
items.reveal:
Poore and Nemecek (2018) aggregated data from over 38,000 farms. For most foods, on-farm emissions, land-use change and processing dominate. Air-freighted produce and beef from deforested land are exceptions.

Choosing what to eat typically dwarfs food miles for footprint.
items.why: Salient measures (miles travelled) can mislead about underlying impacts.
